summary: Ter Ellingson is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as a music professor at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.
Terence Dukes was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Kongoryuji Temple in 1978 and taught there.

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned an M.A. from UCLA. She served at the Asian Art Museum, including as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art (attested 2001–2003).
Terry Kleeman is a Sinology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of British Columbia (~1980–1988) and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998.
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He was a teacher to the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nihon, Tohoku, Keio, Komazawa, and Aichi Universities, and served as president of Tohoku University and Miyagi University of Education.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Florida, FSU, and UVA (PhD ~1991), among other institutions. She taught at UVA and IUPUI before becoming a professor of religion at Florida State University in 1993.
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in history and archaeology. She studied at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He taught as a professor at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1968–1978), and was professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1968–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Berlin. He served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo, professor at Toyo University, and president of Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda and Komazawa Universities. He served in multiple faculty and leadership roles at Komazawa University, including president (2002–2006), and later served as president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi was a scholar in Sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1966–1974), the University of Tsukuba (~1974–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He taught ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and held the ethics chair at the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a philosopher and Japanologist educated at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1924–1931) and served as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).

Teun Goudriaan was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Jan Gonda. He served at Utrecht University, where he is attested as a committee member in 1989 and Professor Emeritus in 2000.
Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Oberlin College and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1976–1986). He founded Metta Forest Monastery and became its abbot in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under guide Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Thatchathon Attarung is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar studying for a Ph.D. at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (2024–2026). In 2024, he was appointed Secretary to the Dean's Office there and Associate Editor at Journal of Applied Humanities Studies.
Theo Murray is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar pursuing a Ph.D. at the Australian National University (attested 2026).
